# Colecto v0.6.0

Extensions were rebuilt from the ground up. Your mail works as before; a few settings
moved, the composer got its own tab, and anything an extension shows now says which
extension it came from.

## What you'll notice

- **The composer has its own tab** next to Reader. Drag it anywhere, like any other
  pane. "Mailbox" and "Message reader" are now simply **Mail** and **Reader**.
- **Some settings moved.** List density and date headings are in **Settings → Mail**.
  Where notifications appear, and whether they also reach your desktop, are in
  **Settings → Appearance**. Mail, Privacy and Notifications settings start from their
  defaults once after updating.
- **Everything says who it's from.** Toasts, extension dialogs and settings pages that
  an extension draws carry its name, so a third-party extension can never pass itself
  off as Colecto.
- **No more "Show notifications" switch.** To silence notifications, turn the
  Notifications extension off in **Settings → Extensions**. Toasts from extensions you
  installed yourself still show.
- **AI labels work in the background.** Automatic labels now run inside the AI
  extension's sandbox whenever new mail arrives, even with no window open. Nothing
  changes in how you set them up. See
  [AI features](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.6.0/docs/ai.md).
- **Opening a message is a little slower**, by roughly 50–70 ms, because the inbox and
  the reader are now separate sandboxed extensions that talk through Colecto. We'll be
  working on that.

## For extension authors

- **A new extension system.** An extension's interface now runs in a sandboxed Web
  Worker on the device, with no DOM and no network. It describes what to show with
  components Colecto draws in its own style, and reaches your mail only through its
  own credential, which Colecto checks on every call. Optional background work runs in
  a WebAssembly service part. Start with
  [Make your own extension](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.6.0/docs/extensions/guide.md)
  and the
  [extension contract](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.6.0/docs/extensions/README.md).
- **API 1, again.** The extension API starts over at
  [API 1](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.6.0/docs/extensions/api-versions/API-1.md).
  Extensions built for the old system (the alpha's API 1 to 3) no longer load: Colecto
  removes them, and their settings, on startup. Reinstall versions built for the new
  system.
- **Panes, settings pages, commands, toasts, dialogs and slots.** Extensions can add a
  workspace pane, a settings page, command-runner entries and search, top-bar buttons,
  toasts, dialogs, and content inside other extensions' slots such as the reader's
  toolbar.
- **A canvas overlay.** The new `ui.canvas` capability gives an extension a
  full-window drawing surface that never takes clicks. The
  [Oneko](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/tree/v0.6.0/docs/extensions/examples/oneko)
  cat is back to show it off.
- **Service parts hear about new mail** and get small key-value storage. See the
  [Rust SDK](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.6.0/docs/extensions/rust-sdk.md).

## Not yet

- The composer is still plain text.
- Client parts can be written in JavaScript or as raw Wasm, but the Rust SDK only
  covers service parts so far.
- The desktop and Android builds of this release were not tried by hand before
  shipping.
